This plot is small, only about a quarter hectare, and it is not even my own land — I rent it, so I will not spend big money on it. For my cassava and cocoyam here in the South South, the rain is plenty and the bush fallow still gives some life to the soil, so I will not buy fertilizer this season — money is tight and one bag is too much for this small piece anyway. I will put some household refuse and goat droppings I gather around the compound, use my own cassava cuttings from last year like my neighbors do, and weed by hand with my children. I may call one or two people to help me with the ridging and planting when the work is too much for my back.
